channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Brasil não vê risco de 'efeito Zelensky' em visita de Lula a Trump
item.description: Brazilian diplomats and Lula's aides dismiss the risk of public embarrassment by Donald Trump during the White House meeting, despite his unpredictable style. They expect the encounter to follow traditional diplomatic norms, avoiding a 'Zelensky effect'.

item.title: Reforma tributária é irreversível e deve estar acima de questões políticas, dizem gestores públicos
item.description: Public officials from the federal government, states, and municipalities state that the tax reform is irreversible and must remain above political considerations, ensuring the continuation of the transition to the new system regardless of who is elected or re-elected in 2026.

item.title: Depois de Pedro, Ancelotti vai ao Nilton Santos ver Danilo
item.description: Brazil national team coach Carlo Ancelotti will visit Estádio Nilton Santos this Wednesday to closely watch Botafogo midfielder Danilo in the match against Racing, along with Alex Telles and Vitinho. This follows his attendance at Flamengo vs Vasco at Maracanã last weekend, where he observed Pedro stand out. The preliminary World Cup squad will be submitted to FIFA on Monday, with the final 26-player list announced on May 18.

item.title: Acordo de delação premiada segue diversas etapas; entenda
item.description: Daniel Vorcaro's defense submitted the annexes of his plea bargain to the Federal Police and the Attorney General's Office on May 5, 2026, following a confidentiality agreement signed in March. The material is now under review by prosecutors and investigators, who may request additional clarifications before potential homologation by the Supreme Federal Court, under Justice André Mendonça's rapporteurship. The plea bargain, governed by Brazil's Organized Crime Law since 2013, poses risks of exposing authorities across the Three Powers and is led by lawyer José Luis Oliveira Lima (Juca), known for defending José Dirceu and Braga Netto.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Lula tem aprovação negativa em 6 dos 10 maiores estados do país
item.description: President Lula has negative approval ratings in six of Brazil's ten largest states, according to data presented on Papo Antagonista. The Chamber of Deputies' Ethics Council also approved a 60-day suspension of the mandates of deputies Marcos Pollon, Marcel van Hattem, and Zé Trovão. Both topics were discussed in Wednesday's episode.

item.title: Moro critica veto de Lula a trecho de lei que aumenta pena para roubo com lesão grave
item.description: Senator Sergio Moro (PL-PR) criticized President Lula's (PT) veto of a provision in Law 15.397/2026 that would have increased penalties for robbery resulting in serious bodily injury. The law, signed on Monday, amends the Penal Code to toughen punishments for crimes including theft, robbery, fraud, and receiving stolen goods. Moro accused the president of once again opposing harsher criminal penalties.

item.title: Lula dispensa hotel e decide se hospedar em outro local em Washington
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva chose to stay at the Brazilian embassy residence in Washington D.C., forgoing a hotel, during his day-trip to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump. Lula will arrive on the evening of Wednesday, May 6, and return to Brazil on the evening of Thursday, May 7, the same day as the White House meeting. He is accompanied by five ministers and the Federal Police director, while First Lady Janja is not joining him.

item.title: Lei permite que médicos residentes fracionem suas férias
item.description: Law 15.400/2026 allows medical residents and other health professionals to split their 30 annual vacation days into periods of at least 10 days each, amending Law 6.932/1981. Originating from Bill 1.732/2022 by former deputy Dra. Soraya Manato, the law was approved by the Senate and signed by President Lula, set to take effect in 180 days. Senator Wilder Morais, who reported the bill in the CAS, emphasized that vacation splitting already exists for most Brazilian workers and incurs no costs for residency programs.

item.title: Senado aprova a proibição de telemarketing de venda por robôs
item.description: The Senate approved a bill banning telemarketing sales conducted by robots or automated recordings without human intervention, with rapporteur Hamilton Mourão. The proposal, authored by Ciro Nogueira, was passed in a terminative decision and proceeds directly to the Chamber of Deputies. An amendment by Eduardo Gomes was accepted to allow phone contacts for security or transparency purposes in contracts, such as 'double verification'.

item.title: Múcio vai a Alcolumbre para ‘baixar temperatura’ de relação com o governo após rejeição de Messias
item.description: Defense Minister José Múcio met with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre at the Senate's Official Residence to ease tensions between the Executive and Legislative branches following the rejection of Jorge Messias as Attorney General. The friendly meeting aimed to restart dialogue between Alcolumbre and President Lula, focusing on institutional stability.

item.title: Ministros reforçam vedação a pagamentos de penduricalhos fora da lista do Supremo
item.description: Ministers Flávio Dino and Alexandre de Moraes reinforced that payments of 'penduricalhos' outside the list authorized by the STF are prohibited, potentially leading to criminal, civil, and administrative liability for public officials. The ruling states that only indemnity payments expressly authorized by the STF and the Time-in-Service Allowance (ATS), each capped at 35% of the constitutional ceiling (R$ 46.366,19), may be paid, with a maximum total of R$ 78.528 for magistrates with advanced careers.

item.title: Lula precisa buscar entendimento em diálogo com Trump
item.description: Lula must seek understanding in dialogue with Trump to strengthen Brazil-U.S. relations, particularly in strategic areas such as trade, organized crime combat, and strategic minerals exploration. Despite a decline in Brazilian exports in 2025 due to the tariff surge, the U.S. remains the third-largest destination for Brazilian goods and the fourth country with the largest U.S. trade surplus. Bilateral cooperation is seen as beneficial for both nations, with potential to expand partnership across multiple sectors.

item.title: Deputadas do Psol propõem redução de jornada de 15% para mães
item.description: Deputadas Fernanda Melchionna and Sâmia Bomfim (Psol) proposed an amendment to a PEC that would reduce working hours by 15% for mothers, in addition to the general reduction, and ban the rehiring of CLT workers as PJ to prevent fraud. The initiative aims to end the 6x1 scale and merge two CCJ-approved PECs establishing a 36-hour workweek, with full wage maintenance and potential benefit to 37 million workers.

item.title: STF: Dino e Moraes criminalizam a criação de novos penduricalhos no Judiciário
item.description: Supreme Court justices Flávio Dino and Alexandre de Moraes have banned the creation of new "penduricalhos" — non-constitutional-ceiling remunerative or indemnity payments — for judges, opening the door to criminal, civil, and administrative liability for officials who violate the ruling, based on a Folha de S.Paulo report revealing eight tribunals created such payments after a prior ban.

item.title: Moraes quer que STF proíba assembleias de derrubarem prisões de deputados
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered the preventive detention of state deputy Thiago Rangel to be maintained, rejecting the Rio de Janeiro Legislative Assembly’s attempt to overturn it. He criticized the automatic use of parliamentary immunity as a tool for impunity, noting that in 13 recent cases of deputies arrested for crimes unrelated to their mandate, 12 were overturned by state assemblies — eight of them in Rio alone. Moraes referred the case to the First Chamber of the STF, arguing the practice enables criminal organizations to infiltrate public office.

item.title: Comissão aprova CNH automática, mas inclui exigência de exames médicos
item.description: The mixed committee approved MP 1.327/2025, known as the 'Good Driver MP', with an amendment maintaining the mandatory medical exam for automatic CNH renewal, contrary to the original government proposal. The text now proceeds to analysis in the Chamber of Deputies plenary. The benefit does not apply to drivers aged 70 or older, nor to those with reduced CNH validity due to medical recommendation.

item.title: Plano de “governo de extrema direita” já está pronto, diz Boulos
item.description: Guilherme Boulos (Psol) claimed the far right already has a ready government plan, composed of proposals from right-aligned politicians that attack workers. He cited statements by Romeu Zema on child labor, Flávio Bolsonaro on exploiting Brazil’s rare earths, Nikolas Ferreira on a supposed 'boss bolsa', and Valdemar Costa Neto, asserting the right seeks fewer rights, less protection, and more exploitation.

item.title: Dino reforça proibição de penduricalhos e alerta para risco de responsabilização penal
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino reinforced the ban on non-statutory 'penduricalhos,' warning that non-compliance may lead to criminal, civil, and administrative liability for judiciary and prosecution officials. In March, the STF capped indemnity payments at 35% above the constitutional ceiling of R$ 46,000. The ruling nullified benefits like housing and childcare allowances, despite subsequent CNJ and CNMP regulations in April.

item.title: Lula recebeu ligação de Trump antes de viagem aos EUA; governo avaliou conversa como 'amistosa'
item.description: Lula received a friendly phone call from Trump on Friday (1st), during which the Brazilian president made himself available for an in-person meeting in the U.S., scheduled for Thursday (7th). The call lasted about 40 minutes, with Trump praising Lula’s political trajectory and ending with an 'I love you'. The meeting aims to normalize bilateral trade relations and discuss topics including organized crime, critical minerals, geopolitics, and Brazilian elections.

item.title: Jaques Wagner diz que Messias foi usado para dar 'cacetada' em Lula
item.description: Jaques Wagner, the government leader in the Senate, said that the failed nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court was used by many as a way to 'hit' President Lula, describing the episode as a 'bludgeoning' against the government.

item.title: Paulinho da Força descarta repetir chapa presidencial com Ciro Gomes: ‘dá muito trabalho’, diz
item.description: Paulinho da Força ruled out running as a presidential running mate with Ciro Gomes in 2026, saying the idea 'takes too much work'. He had discussed the possibility with Aécio Neves but reversed course, advocating for an alternative candidacy to leading figures like Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, and criticizing the 'third way' as being too far to the right.

item.title: Em novas decisões, Dino e Moraes reiteram proibição de criação e pagamento de penduricalhos
item.description: Supreme Court ministers Flávio Dino and Alexandre de Moraes reaffirmed the absolute ban on creating and paying 'penduricalhos' in the public sector, stating only explicitly authorized benefits may be paid. Dino emphasized the prohibition applies to benefits created after the March 25, 2026 ruling and mandated monthly transparency reports, with officials facing penal, civil, and administrative liability for non-compliance.

item.title: PSDB quer decidir até o fim de maio sobre candidatura de Paulo Serra ao governo de SP
item.description: The PSDB aims to decide by the end of May whether Paulo Serra, former mayor of Santo André, will run for governor of São Paulo in 2026. Serra’s allies report internal division, with roughly a 50% chance he will either pursue or withdraw from the race, due to concerns about lacking a strong alliance network that could make the candidacy electorally suicidal. While some party factions believe a standalone bid could boost proportional representation and expand the federal delegation, others warn it could lead to electoral defeat without solid backing.

item.title: Bolsonaristas reclamam de retenção de recursos do PL para agendas e publicidade de Flávio
item.description: Allies of Jair Bolsonaro complain about the slow disbursement of PL party funds for Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, particularly affecting advertising and travel logistics in May. The complaints were directed to PL national president Valdemar Costa Neto and reflect internal disagreements over Flávio’s chosen marketing team.

item.title: Reunião Lula-Trump: 'pancadaria' ou 'troca de afagos'?
item.description: Former Brazilian external debt negotiator and ex-ambassador to the European Union, Jorio Dauster, expresses concern over the upcoming meeting between Lula and Donald Trump, suggesting the encounter could be marked by tension or confrontation, using the term 'pancadaria' to imply potential hostility. He warns that despite surface-level cordiality, there are substantial risks in bilateral relations due to deep ideological and political differences between the two leaders.

item.title: Jaques Wagner diz que relação com Alcolumbre estremeceu: ‘Ele queria o Pacheco’
item.description: The Senate government leader, Jaques Wagner (PT-BA), stated that his relationship with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) became strained after the rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF. Wagner said Alcolumbre preferred Rodrigo Pacheco for the seat and worked behind the scenes to secure Messias’ defeat, which failed with 34 votes in favor and 42 against — short of the 41 needed. Wagner accused the opposition of orchestrating a political maneuver to 'deliver a blow' to Lula, turning the hearing into an ideological clash.

item.title: Saiba como regularizar o título de eleitor sem sair de casa
item.description: Voters across Brazil can regularize their voter registration online until 11:59 PM on May 6, 2026, through the TSE's Autoatendimento Eleitoral (Título Net) system, without visiting a notary office. The service enables first-time issuance, address transfer, data updates, and debt clearance, especially for those with biometric registration. After the deadline, the electoral roll closes, and those not in compliance will be barred from voting and may face restrictions on obtaining passports, holding public office, or enrolling in public educational institutions.

item.title: Toffoli rejeita habeas corpus para soltar Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Dias Toffoli rejected a habeas corpus petition seeking to release former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year-and-three-month sentence for leading a coup attempt, currently under house arrest for health reasons. Toffoli emphasized that Bolsonaro has regular legal representation and that the petition could interfere with his defense strategy. The decision maintains Bolsonaro’s house arrest pending a new evaluation after the 90-day period granted by Minister Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: PESQUISA PRESIDENTE! LULA OU FLÁVIO? BIG DATA X MEIO IDEIA: EM QUAL CONFIAR? MAIO 2026
item.description: The content appears to be a YouTube video about a presidential poll for the 2026 Brazilian elections, mentioning a comparison between Lula and Flávio (likely Flávio Bolsonaro or another candidate with that name). The video questions the reliability between big data and 'gut feeling' (intuition), suggesting a debate over electoral research methodologies. No specific poll results or candidate proposals are detailed.

item.title: Direita dominou debates nas redes sociais na última semana, diz instituto
item.description: The right dominated social media debates between April 27 and May 4, leading in four of the six most discussed topics, according to Instituto Democracia em Xeque. The left was ahead only on federal social programs (54%) and in framing the dosimetry bill as an amnesty for Bolsonaro and heinous crimes (73%). The study analyzed 172,909 posts with 260.8 million interactions across Facebook, Instagram, X, YouTube, and TikTok.

item.title: Genial/Quaest: presidenciáveis, Caiado lidera disputa em GO, enquanto Zema fica atrás de Lula e Flávio em MG
item.description: In Goiás, former governor Ronaldo Caiado leads the presidential race with 31% in the first round and 51% in a potential runoff against Lula, reflecting strong state-level approval (84%). In Minas Gerais, Romeu Zema trails with just 11% in the first round, behind Lula (33%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (27%), as his approval drops to 52%. The Genial/Quaest poll shows that despite their state-level standing, neither candidate is competitive nationally, with Lula and the Bolsonaro family dominating voter intentions in both states.

item.title: Recursos de Cláudio Castro no TSE podem ser julgados por nova formação de ministros na Corte
item.description: The declaration appeals filed by Cláudio Castro's defense may be judged by a new TSE formation, as rapporteur Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva took over the case after Isabel Gallotti's departure, who had already voted. The case's inclusion in the agenda will depend on the new Court president, Minister Nunes Marques, who assumes office on February 12. The defense seeks annulment of the judgment and suspension of the conviction for abuse of power, while the Electoral Public Ministry highlights a contradiction between the ruling and the formal omission of the diploma's cassation.

item.title: Defesa de Daniela Mercury insiste que STF torne Eduardo Bolsonaro réu por difamação
item.description: Daniela Mercury's defense has urged the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to indict Eduardo Bolsonaro for defamation, claiming he made false and offensive statements against the singer. The request was reiterated in an exclusive article available only to subscribers. The case centers on allegations that Bolsonaro abused his position to damage Mercury's reputation.

item.title: Político ou técnico? Como os brasileiros acham que deve ser o novo ministro do STF
item.description: A survey reveals that 39.4% of Brazilians prefer a technical, non-government-affiliated nominee for the STF, while 37% support a candidate with direct government ties, such as Jorge Messias. Messias’s Senate rejection was seen by 36% as opposition sabotage and by 35% as government weakness, reflecting deep division over the ideal profile for the Supreme Court vacancy.

item.title: Motta diz que ida do PT à Justiça é direito, mas defende dosimetria
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta said the PT has the right to appeal to the STF against the overturning of Lula’s veto on the dosimetry law for January 8 crimes, but stressed that Congress’s decision should be upheld. He called the bill a chance for national pacification. The law benefits Jair Bolsonaro and 849 others convicted in the 2023 attacks.

item.title: Após derrota dupla no Congresso, Lula falta aos 200 anos da Câmara
item.description: President Lula did not attend the Chamber's 200th anniversary ceremony following two congressional defeats: the rejection of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Court and the overturning of his veto on the Dosimetry Bill. He was represented by Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães before traveling to the U.S. to meet with Donald Trump. His absence highlights the growing disconnect between the Planalto and Congress in 2026, with no recorded meetings with congressional leaders so far this year.

item.title: Por encontro com Trump, Lula embarca para os Estados Unidos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva departed for the United States on Wednesday to meet with Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday. The meeting aims to restore trade relations strained by U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods and will cover cooperation against organized crime, critical minerals, geopolitics, and Brazilian elections. Lula noted Vice President Geraldo Alckmin will assume presidential duties during his absence.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro pode se lançar a suplente de senador mesmo vivendo nos EUA?
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro plans to run as a Senate substitute for São Paulo while living in the U.S., despite being stripped of office and facing criminal charges at the STF for coercion related to the coup attempt. Although there is no immediate legal barrier, his candidacy hinges on the timing of a final conviction: if upheld before the election, it could trigger supervenient ineligibility and block his diploma.

item.title: Especialista explica o que muda para Bolsonaro após derrubada de veto ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: The overturning of the presidential veto on the Dosimetria Bill allows for sentence reduction for those convicted in the January 8 acts, including Jair Bolsonaro, through the application of beneficial retroactivity in criminal law. However, constitutional expert Acácio Miranda notes that the new law requires a formal manifestation from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to grant benefits, making the process more bureaucratic and a rapid release unlikely — Bolsonaro is expected to remain imprisoned for at least three or four years. President Lula’s decision not to promulgate the law leaves room for political and judicial debate, while a potential future amnesty by another president could change the scenario, though this falls outside the scope of the Dosimetria Bill discussion.

item.title: Hugo Motta é contra a criação de estatal para minerais críticos
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta opposed the creation of a state-owned company, Terrabras, to explore critical minerals, advocating instead for strengthening the National Council of Mineral Policy and Rare Earths as a means to ensure national sovereignty without compromising private investment. He argued that the council model fulfills the government’s strategy of maintaining state control over strategic resources without establishing a public enterprise. The Terrabras proposal, initially considered by the Lula administration, was postponed and has since lost momentum, with current focus shifting to regulatory adjustments and export restriction mechanisms.

item.title: Desenrola cria cultura que ignora razão do endividamento recorde, diz pesquisador do 'Brasil dos boletos'
item.description: Researcher Kauê Lopes dos Santos from 'Brasil dos boletos' states that while the Desenrola 2.0 program is an important government response to indebtedness, it may foster a culture of debt renegotiation that overlooks structural causes of credit dependency in Brazil, focusing only on short-term solutions.

item.title: Ministro da articulação política de Lula se reúne com Alcolumbre uma semana após derrota de Messias
item.description: Political Articulation Minister José Guimarães met with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to ease tensions between the Lula government and Congress, one week after the defeat of Jorge Messias in the STF nomination and the overturning of the Dosimetry bill veto. The meeting aimed to 'turn the page' on recent parliamentary setbacks, with Guimarães stressing that the government is not over and advocating for calm, non-resentful engagement.

item.title: Depois de reveses, Guimarães elogia convivência democrática na Câmara
item.description: Minister José Guimarães praised democratic coexistence in the Chamber of Deputies during the 200th anniversary celebration, highlighting his 20 years as a federal deputy and emphasizing that Parliament has overcome difficult moments, such as the Military Dictatorship and January 8. He made these remarks following two legislative defeats for the Lula government: the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF and Congress overturning Lula’s veto on the Dosimetria bill, which reduces penalties for coup-related crimes.

item.title: Governador interino do RJ é aprovado por 52,9%, diz pesquisa
item.description: The Futura/Apex poll shows that interim Rio de Janeiro Governor Ricardo Couto has 52.9% approval and 38.5% disapproval, with 31.6% rating his administration as excellent or good. Conducted between April 22–24 among 1,000 voters, the survey has a 3.1-point margin of error and 95% confidence level. Couto assumed office following resignations in the succession line, including former Governor Cláudio Castro, and his continuation in office was ordered by STF Minister Cristiano Zanin, pending a decision on a supplementary election by January 2027.

item.title: Pilili, a inútil
item.description: The TSE launched Pilili, an electronic ballot box mascot, to celebrate 30 years of electronic voting and engage younger voters. Though visually simple and childlike, the initiative aims to make the electoral process more accessible and playful for new generations. The post criticizes the mascot as 'useless' and overly juvenile, likening it to kindergarten-level design.

item.title: Lula deixa Brasília e decola para encontro com Trump na Casa Branca
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva departed for Washington on Wednesday afternoon to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump on Thursday. The agenda includes discussions on trade tariffs, the potential designation of Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist organizations, the war in Iran, critical mineral exploration, and the situation in Venezuela. Lula is accompanied by ministers of Foreign Affairs, Justice, Finance, Development, Mines and Energy, and the director-general of the Federal Police.

item.title: É #FAKE que Lula disse que 'vai embora para Cuba' se Flávio Bolsonaro vencer eleições
item.description: False posts circulating on social media claim President Lula said he would 'move to Cuba' if Flávio Bolsonaro wins the 2026 presidential election. There is no official record of such a statement, and the Presidency’s Secretariat of Communication (Secom) has denied it outright. In an interview with Der Spiegel, Lula stated he would accept the people's decision, regardless of the outcome.

item.title: Participação de adolescentes no eleitorado pode atingir pior nível desde 2014, segundo projeção
item.description: The deadline for issuing voter IDs ends this Wednesday (June 6), and Brazil is projected to record the lowest participation rate of 16- and 17-year-olds in a presidential election since at least 2014. This low youth engagement may reflect political disaffection, lack of information, or bureaucratic barriers, affecting the representativeness of the electorate.

item.title: Motta diz que Câmara dará 'grande contribuição' para acordo entre Lula e Trump se aprovar projeto sobre terras-raras
item.description: Hugo Motta, president of the Chamber of Deputies, stated that approving the National Critical Minerals Policy — which includes up to R$5 billion in fiscal incentives and a R$2 billion guarantee fund — would be a 'major contribution' to Lula-Trump negotiations on rare earths. Reporter Arnaldo Jardim called the bill a 'trump card' in talks with the U.S., noting it creates favorable rules for foreign investment and technology transfer. The bill is set for vote Wednesday, with rare earths expected to be discussed in the Lula-Trump meeting Thursday.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reforça defesa de redução de maioridade penal com gradações de 14 e 16 anos
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for President of Brazil, reinforced his defense of lowering the age of criminal responsibility in Brazil, proposing graduated thresholds of 14 and 16 years. His statements align with a broader agenda of penal hardening, consistent with his political faction's positions.
